gaps.sentence: The ___ repairs were making the theatre impossible to run profitably.
This small car is very ___ to run.
gaps.explanation: 'Economical' means costing little or saving money; 'economic' relates to trade, industry or the economy.

gaps.sentence: This smell ___ me of my childhood.
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody of something' means to make someone think of something; 'remember' is not followed by an object + of.

gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: The government plans to ___ taxes next year.
gaps.hint: the verb takes an object: taxes
gaps.explanation: 'Raise' means to lift or increase something (takes an object); 'rise' means to go up (no object).

gaps.sentence: One of the bolts had worked ___ in the vibration.
gaps.explanation: 'Work loose' = become untightened; 'lose' is the verb for misplacing.

gaps.sentence: The two brothers are ___ in appearance but not in character.
gaps.explanation: 'They are alike' — 'alike' follows the verb and cannot come before a noun.

gaps.sentence: She ___ the documents on the desk and left.
gaps.hint: past of the verb meaning 'put down' (takes an object)
gaps.explanation: 'Laid' is the past of 'lay' (put something down), which takes an object: she laid the documents.
